newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks power ahead at close.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa swept higher at the close Monday, driven by strong foreign bidding in key blue-chip stocks, dealers said.

"There is very strong interest by foreign investors on the back of last week's record number of corporate purchases," said Leonardo Torres Barsanti at Rio Research. "However, because prices and volume have grown so much we should be very cautious near-term on the bolsa -- a downward correction would actually be healthy."
The blue-chip MerVal index, which has fallen only twice in the past three weeks, rose 1.8 percent to 792.09.
Floor volume remained strong at 39.4 million pesos compared to 40.2 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover soared to 315.7 million pesos compared to 171.5 million pesos.
"OTC surged on a buying spree in stocks like Banco de Galicia, which remains the gem among banks which has not been touched yet," another trader said.

Banco Frances, Banco Rio de la Plata and Banco Roberts recently announced mergers brokered by foreign investment groups but Banco de Galicia, previously the country's biggest private bank, "remains up for grabs," the dealer said.
Banco de Galicia jumped 3.9 percent in the session while Banco del Suquia, Bansud and Banco Frances, the three only other listed banks, rallied 6.8 percent, 3.8 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.
The broad market index matched MerVal gains of 3.8 percent, with winners smashing losers 59 to seven and 20 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were carmaker Ciadea, steelmaker Siderar and holding company Comercial del Plata, which shot up 6.3 percent, 5.0 percent and 4.6 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were foods giant Molinos and construction stock Polledo, which eased 0.5 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively.
